scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (eight engineers)

motion.text: The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on every repository.

research: Priya: Pull old suppress-comment count from six-month Lintwise usage to produce a concrete false-positive percentage per rule category.

Marcus: Run a one-week shadow pass on the monorepo to measure (a) Lintwise wall-clock time on changed files, (b) whether existing CI runners have spare capacity to launch it as a parallel job at the 2 PM peak queue, and (c) resulting queue-depth impact.
Elena: Pull Lintwise's published ruleset and confirm it ships secret-detection patterns (API keys, tokens, private keys) and a dependency-vulnerability check; report coverage gaps.
Sana: Run a timed shadow check on one SQL-heavy pipeline repo to confirm Lintwise parses .sql files without dialect false positives and measure added latency against her specific workload.
Lars: Review the shadow-run output for measured false-positive rate per rule category; flag any rule emitting noise above ~5%.
Jin: Aggregate shadow-run wall-clock and FP data; confirm the lint step stays under 15 s in parallel before endorsing a hard merge gate.
Olga: Review shadow-run findings on a sample PR to judge whether the feedback is clear and actionable for a junior dev, or noisy enough to cause confusion.

chairQuestions.topic: Measured wall-clock runtime and false-positive rate of Lintwise during six months of daily use
chairQuestions.experience_sought: I need concrete numbers: how many seconds did Lintwise typically take on a changed-files run versus a full-repo run, and roughly what percentage of its findings turned out to be false positives that required a manual suppress or ignore comment?

chairQuestions.topic: Current CI infrastructure's ability to run a parallel lint job alongside the 11-minute build
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Can you confirm whether the existing CI runners have spare capacity to launch Lintwise as a parallel job next to the build step without increasing queue wait time, and what the current peak queue depth looks like around 2 PM?
